verdict.rationale: Anytype documents two ways to run without its cloud. Local-only mode disables Anytype's backup node entirely, and self-hosting uses your own network configuration with a team-maintained docker image. Both sit on an offline-first, device-local storage model, and a community user reports that P2P sync works fine. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of running the self-hosted sync backend, and a smoother migration path (switching network mode requires exporting and re-importing into a new identity; local-only sync is limited to the same LAN).

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole system without the vendor's cloud — local-only mode or a self-hosted sync backend I operate myself

citations.quote: you can enable local-only mode. This mode disables Anytype's backup node entirely
If you prefer to fully keep your data on your device without any server to sync between your desktop and mobile, you can enable local-only mode.
To back up your channels and data to a self-hosted network, you need to have a network configuration... There's also a docker image that's maintained by the team.
All your content is stored locally on your device... This means an offline-first experience: the app always works without an internet connection
You can work completely offline, sync across your own devices, or self-host your data.
